notes.title: Multiplayer limit increase
notes.notes:
[h1]Changes[/h1]
[list]
[*] Increased the limit of multiplayer lobbies to 250
[/list]
[h1]Notes[/h1]
This change was requested during yesterdays event. The goal of this change is to make it easier for trees to reach the 100 tree forest achievement and not prevent more than 100 trees from joining. Because of the original intent, only 100 trees will ever spawn, after 100 more players will join the lobby but the number of physical trees will remain the same.

I have not really tested this because I do not have 100 computers, but I may schedule another "Developer tree time" event for TS2023 and TS2022 at the same time for the purposes of testing this achievement, achieving it for those who requested it yesterday and probably talking about my new game which everyone should wishlist to support my work in general. The amount of time I can spend on TS2024 development next year will be directly affected by my work on this game, so please be patient, it will likely be later in the year if / when I can spend time on it:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2244830/Nautikin_Adventures/?curator_clanid=41985425

notes.title: Tree Fact #9012
notes.notes:
Did you know?

Due to minor variations in trees, some apple trees grow larger (or smaller) apples than others. For example, the largest apple on record weighed around 4lbs and was grown in a normal sized apple tree in Japan. One could only assume that you could grow apple trees specifically for creating larger and larger apples similar to the way that we grow trees with the goal of producing tastier and better looking apples for marketing purposes. Though apparently over time this has resulted in a decrease in natural nutrients found in the apples. This would also apply to similar fruit trees.

https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/heaviest-apple
https://heated.medium.com/todays-apple-may-contain-38-percent-fewer-nutrients-than-the-same-one-in-1950-530d885a07f1

notes.title: Tree Fact #2015
notes.notes:
Did you know?

Some trees face constant winds as they grow. This forces the tree to grow in a bent shape over time giving these windswept trees a unique appearance.

notes.title: Tree Fact #889145
notes.notes:
Did you know?

There are many ancient trees! The Nothofagus moorei (aka Antarctic beech tree) can be found in a few different locations around the globe (most notably rain forests). Given the extreme ages (2000+ years) of these trees the soil and physical characteristics of these trees are usually unique and stand out in an otherwise ubiquitous variation. It's interesting to think that one could mount an expedition to an old forest rarely visited and probably find a tree no living person has ever seen before (maybe previously unknown). Surely finding a tree of similar significance would be a life long achievement (at least for the sentimental).

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nothofagus_moorei
https://www.monumentaltrees.com/en/aus/mainland/queensland/16423_repeaterstationroad/
https://trusttrees.org.au/tree/QLD/Springbrook/Repeater_Station_Road

notes.title: Double Tree Fact #71983 & #71284
notes.notes:
Did you know?

The Rainbow Eucalyptus tree grows so fast that it's bark does not peel off at the same rate creating a colorful appearance. It is considered an invasive species by many and has a life span of 150 years.

https://www.worldatlas.com/articles/rainbow-eucalyptus-you-can-visit-the-most-colorful-tree-on-earth.html

Also,

The Strangler Fig strangles older trees by growing around them for years until they ultimately die.

https://www.worldatlas.com/articles/why-is-the-strangler-fig-tree-called-so.html

notes.title: Tree Fact #71984
notes.notes:
Did you know?

Kangaroos don't just hop around the outback. They also live in trees! Almost exclusively in fact. 
They can leap 30 feet from tree to tree in the rain forest and lick their arms to stay cool in the heat.

https://www.worldatlas.com/articles/tree-kangaroo-facts-animals-of-oceania.html

notes.title: Tree Fact #22059
notes.notes:
Did you know?

The hardest tree in the world is known as the Bull-oak or Allocasuarina luehmannii (short name!). It's wood is said to have a Janka hardness of 22,500 N and is native to the east side of Australia.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allocasuarina_luehmannii
https://wtlandcare.org/details/allocasuarina-luehmannii/

notes.title: Tree Fact #10811
notes.notes:
Did you know? 

Some trees grow fruit that is poisonous to humans. The Manchineel tree grows small green fruit very similar in appearance to an apple that will almost certainly result in death if mistaken for one. Beware! 

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchineel
https://www.worldatlas.com/articles/which-is-the-most-dangerous-tree-in-the-world.html

notes.title: Tree Fact #8849
notes.notes:
The Scoctra tree (aka Dragon's blood tree) aside from having an awesome name and visual appearance has red tree sap and only grows on a group islands miles off the cost of Yemen. 

https://www.worldatlas.com/articles/where-is-socotra-located.html

notes.title: Tree Fact #4252
notes.notes:
Did you know?

Baobab trees can store 30k+ gallons of water in order to survive and can grow 100 feet tall!

https://www.worldatlas.com/articles/the-species-of-baobab-trees.html
